title: Mapping objects and pointwise tensors in enriched cotensors
statement:
Use the universe and complete enriched-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the internal enriched functors, free enrichment and cotensors of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus], and the twisted-arrow construction with source and target $(s,t):\operatorname{Tw}(K)\to K^{\mathrm{op}}\times K$ of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Let $\mathcal V$ be a presentably closed symmetric monoidal infinity category, let $\mathcal E$ be a small complete $\mathcal V$-category, and let $K$ be a small infinity category. Put $\mathcal E^K=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(K_{\mathcal V},\mathcal E)$. For coherent diagrams $F,G:K\to U\mathcal E$ there is a natural equivalence in $\mathcal V$
$$\mathcal E^K(F,G)\simeq\lim_{(k\to k')\in\operatorname{Tw}(K)}\mathcal E(F(k),G(k')).$$
The diagram on the right uses enriched precomposition by $F$ and postcomposition by $G$. Its projections at identity arrows agree with component evaluation, and the comparison retains enriched composition and all naturality parameter simplices.

Suppose in addition that $\mathcal E$ is coherently tensored over $\mathcal V$: for every $A\in\mathcal V$ and $x\in\mathcal E$ there is $A\odot x$ with natural equivalences $\mathcal E(A\odot x,y)\simeq[A,\mathcal E(x,y)]_{\mathcal V}$, compatible with the tensor unit, associativity and evaluation. Then $\mathcal E^K$ is tensored, with $(A\odot F)(k)=A\odot F(k)$ and its induced coherent arrow action. The natural equivalences
$$\mathcal E^K(A\odot F,G)\simeq[A,\mathcal E^K(F,G)]_{\mathcal V}$$
identify the tensor evaluation with its objectwise evaluations, including all parameter simplices. No dualizability assumption on $A$ is imposed. Empty $K$ is allowed. The assertions hold for simplicial indexing shapes after their freely generated infinity categories are used.

source.place: Remark 9.5 for the complete internal enriched functor category, supplemented by the agent-formulated enriched cotensor end and pointwise tensor calculation. Compare the ordinary weighted-end description in Riehl--Verity, Homotopy coherent adjunctions, section 5.1, and the space-valued analogue lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula. Neither source is claimed to state this full V-valued package verbatim; archival copies WANTED. No Stacks tag states it.

proof.text: Write $M=\mathcal E^K(F,G)$. The enriched Hom bifunctor supplied by [lem-coef-collage-crossing-transformations], restricted along $F^{\mathrm{op}}\times G$ and the twisted-arrow projection, gives the coherent diagram $D(f:k\to k')=\mathcal E(Fk,Gk')$ in $\mathcal V$. Its action is precisely enriched precomposition and postcomposition. By the degreewise construction of $\operatorname{Tw}$ it is small when $K$ is small. The complete enriched-category calculus supplies all small limits in $\mathcal V$, so put $L=\lim_{\operatorname{Tw}(K)}D$. For a testing object $v\in\mathcal V$, form $H_v(x,y)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,\mathcal E(x,y))$ and its collage $C_v$. The endpoint categories $U\mathcal E$ and the mixed mapping spaces are small in the fixed smaller universe; the containing universe is used for the category of all testing objects.

source.place: Remark 9.5 supplies the internal Hom framework; agent construction of the test diagram using the cited collage assertion.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-collage-crossing-transformations] with $S=K$, $P=F$ and $Q=G$. It identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,M)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,C_v)}(F_0,G_1)$. Apply the space-valued end formula to this latter functor category. The collage statement identifies each mixed mapping space and its two actions with $H_v$. Consequently
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,M)\simeq\lim_{f\in\operatorname{Tw}(K)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,D(f))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,L).$$
The last equivalence is preservation of limits by the covariant representable, as stated in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. All comparisons are natural in $v,F,G,K$ and in the additional simplicial parameters: the collage and end statements give these compatibilities for their entire mapping spaces, and the representable limit comparison is natural in its diagram and testing object.

source.place: Example 8.3.4.22, applied to the mixed endpoint diagrams; agent passage from all testing spaces to V-valued mapping objects.

proof.text: The fully faithful Yoneda functor of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], applied to $\mathcal V$, turns the natural equivalence of representable presheaves in step 2 into an equivalence $c_{F,G}:M\simeq L$ in $\mathcal V$. Its projection at $f:k\to k'$ sends a parameterized transformation $\alpha$ to $G(f)\alpha_k$, equivalently $\alpha_{k'}F(f)$ with the naturality simplex. At $f=\mathrm{id}_k$ this is component evaluation, since the collage equivalence sends a map to its crossing labels and the end equivalence projects to component evaluation. Applying the same Yoneda full faithfulness to parameter diagrams gives coherent naturality of $c$ in those diagrams, rather than merely naturality of its homotopy class.

source.place: Example 8.3.4.22 identity-arrow evaluation; agent Yoneda reconstruction of the tested equivalence.

proof.text:
The comparison retains enriched composition. For three diagrams $F,G,H$, let $p_f$ be the $f$-projection of $\mathcal E^K(F,G)$ under $c$, and $q_f$ the corresponding projection of $\mathcal E^K(G,H)$. The $f:k\to k'$ projection of the composite is
$$\mathcal E^K(G,H)\otimes\mathcal E^K(F,G)\xrightarrow{q_{\mathrm{id}_{k'}}\otimes p_f}\mathcal E(Gk',Hk')\otimes\mathcal E(Fk,Gk')\longrightarrow\mathcal E(Fk,Hk').$$
Indeed enriched evaluation, which is an enriched functor by [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus], sends composition to composition at $k'$; precomposing by $F(f)$ gives this expression by the naturality simplex from step 3. The endpoint composition, unit and naturality simplices make these maps a cone, including their higher compatibilities. The universal property of the limit, tested by representables as in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], identifies that cone with the composite. Identities give the identity components by the same evaluation formula. This describes the actual composition under the comparison; it does not assume that tensoring preserves the limits.

source.place: Remark 9.5, internal enriched evaluation; agent calculation of the composition cone from the comparison already proved.

proof.text:
Now assume the coherent tensor action in the statement. For fixed $A$, its object assignment $T_A(x)=A\odot x$ has enriched arrow action adjoint to
$$\mathcal E(x,y)\odot(A\odot x)\simeq A\odot(\mathcal E(x,y)\odot x)\xrightarrow{A\odot\mathrm{ev}}A\odot y.$$
Here the equivalence uses tensor associativity and the symmetry in $\mathcal V$; the adjunction is the stipulated tensor universal property with testing object $\mathcal E(x,y)$. Evaluation and the assumed coherent unit and associativity identities show that an identity is sent to an identity and a composite to the composite of these maps, with the same identities on every higher parameter simplex. Thus postcomposition of $F$ with $T_A$ is a coherent diagram $T_AF$, with $(T_AF)(k)=A\odot F(k)$ and arrow action $A\odot F(f)$. The free-enrichment/cotensor identification of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] makes it an object of $\mathcal E^K$. The unit and associativity identifications of this action on diagrams are the given ones at each object and arrow.

source.place: Agent construction directly from the coherent tensor hypothesis and the free-enrichment/cotensor identification; not claimed as a theorem stated in Remark 9.5.

proof.text:
For any small diagram $D:J\to\mathcal V$, the canonical map $[A,\lim_JD]\to\lim_J[A,D(-)]$ is an equivalence. To check this, test at $B\in\mathcal V$ and use closedness and the representable limit criterion:
$$\operatorname{Map}(B,[A,\lim D])\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B\otimes A,\lim D)\simeq\lim_j\operatorname{Map}(B\otimes A,Dj)\simeq\lim_j\operatorname{Map}(B,[A,Dj]).$$
The cited Yoneda limit criterion proves the claim, including its naturality and the empty diagram. Apply the already proved end formula to $T_AF,G$. The stipulated tensor equivalences $\mathcal E(A\odot Fk,Gk')\simeq[A,\mathcal E(Fk,Gk')]$ are coherent equivalences of the twisted-arrow diagrams by their naturality in both variables. Therefore
$$\mathcal E^K(T_AF,G)\simeq\lim_f[A,D(f)]\simeq[A,\lim_fD(f)]\simeq[A,\mathcal E^K(F,G)].$$
This is the required enriched tensor universal property. Only closedness was used to move $[A,-]$ through the limit; $A$ need not be dualizable.

source.place: Agent tensor-Hom/limit calculation using the representable limit criterion; no further enriched-end theorem invoked.

proof.text: The evaluation $A\to\mathcal E^K(F,T_AF)$ is the transpose of $\mathrm{id}_{T_AF}$ under step 6. Projecting at $\mathrm{id}_k$ gives the transpose of $\mathrm{id}_{A\odot Fk}$, namely the specified objectwise tensor evaluation $A\to\mathcal E(Fk,A\odot Fk)$. Every equivalence in step 6 comes from the natural tensor adjunction or a universal cone, so these projections retain all parameter simplices and their faces and degeneracies; they also respect the unit and associativity comparisons of step 5. If $K$ is empty, $\operatorname{Tw}(K)$ is empty, $L$ is terminal in $\mathcal V$, and $[A,L]$ is terminal by step 6; the unique empty diagram consequently satisfies the same tensor property. For a simplicial shape use its freely generated infinity category throughout; the cotensor calculus explicitly supplies that interpretation. Thus the argument applies without imposing nonemptiness or truncating coherent simplices.

source.place: Agent evaluation and edge-case verification using the cotensor and simplicial-shape clauses of the cited calculus.

split_report.summary: Derived the V-valued end by testing with arbitrary v and the existing collage crossing-transformation comparison, space-valued twisted-arrow formula and Yoneda/limit criterion. Constructed the pointwise tensor arrow action, calculated its universal property, composition and evaluation, and checked arbitrary parameters, empty K and simplicial shapes. No new nodes or statement changes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NG-31349ba5c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item: the statement and all 7 steps. I also read the full statements of the 6 nodes it uses and the 3 it depends on, its parent lem-coef-enriched-simplicial-presentation (steps 8-9), and the unit record. Sources read online: Haugseng arXiv:2311.13362v1 Remark 9.5 only gives the closed structure and the internal Hom FUN^V, and the item's source field correctly marks the end and tensor formulas as agent-formulated. Kerodon 03P7 (Example 8.3.4.22) gives the space-valued twisted-arrow limit and matches lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula. Delivery shape: one commit with no new nodes; the statement and blueprint ancestry are unchanged; proof_deps equals the union of the uses. Every cited node is unmerged and in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed. There is no cycle (BFS over 1242 nodes) and no SGA citation. Step checks: step 1 uses the bifunctor clause of the collage node, and the smallness bookkeeping is right. Step 2's hypotheses hold for the collage node (S=K), the end node (C_v is small) and the bimodule clause (the mixed actions agree including higher compatibilities); the end node is not explicitly natural in C_v as v varies, but step 3's identity-arrow projections fix the map, so this is acceptable. Step 3 is Yoneda full faithfulness. In step 4 I checked the composition types by hand: projection = q_{id_k'}(beta) composed with p_f(alpha). In step 5 the transpose of E(x,y)⊙(A⊙x)≃A⊙(E(x,y)⊙x)→A⊙y is correct. Step 6 proves [A,-] preserves limits from closedness alone, with no dualizability of A. Step 7 handles evaluation and empty K. Small cases tested: K empty, a point, and Δ^1 (pullback E(F0,G0)×_{E(F0,G1)}E(F1,G1)); A the unit and A initial. All hold, and the statement is true and not weakened. lem-coef-flexible-weight-enriched-lift also states the end formula as one clause, but it cannot be cited (it would make a cycle through the parent) and it is not a duplicate of the whole item; noted. One problem I did not change, in the existing statement and size conventions rather than this delivery: a V-category with a small object space that is tensored over all of a presentable V is forced to be degenerate (Freyd's argument), so the tensored clause has content only if universes are re-chosen. This is worth a universe note in the coefficient foundation and touches the parent's step 9. No fixes.
